builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
summary: Replaces static, contamination-prone financial benchmarks with a continuously refreshable Japanese benchmark built by a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline that converts heterogeneous certification exams. Costs are per-edition human verification effort, maintenance of exam-specific conversion code, and API spend if the reader evaluates proprietary models; it is an evaluation asset, not a capability improvement. It can fail through conversion errors that slip past review, edition-to-edition drift that breaks comparability, and limited transfer if the reader's production tasks are not Japanese financial QA.
rationale: The benchmark and released pipeline are directly usable on constrained infrastructure to select models for Japanese financial work, but its value depends on whether that domain and its 321-example scope match the reader's production workload.
technique: Refreshable certification-exam benchmark via agentic pipeline

claims.statement: Replaces static, contamination-prone financial benchmarks with a continuously refreshable Japanese benchmark built by a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline that converts heterogeneous certification exams. Costs are per-edition human verification effort, maintenance of exam-specific conversion code, and API spend if the reader evaluates proprietary models; it is an evaluation asset, not a capability improvement. It can fail through conversion errors that slip past review, edition-to-edition drift that breaks comparability, and limited transfer if the reader's production tasks are not Japanese financial QA.

Best open-weight model (Kimi K3.1 Pro) trails the top proprietary model (Claude Fable 5) by 12 percentage points; with terminal and web access every model improves and the gap narrows to about 4 points, with rankings largely unchanged.
